question: Should exact requester adoption of descendant output terminally satisfy descendant delivery even when the requester's outward send later fails?
rationale: The patch changes the meaning of `delivery.status` from visible or final delivery to also include internal requester consumption; source correctness alone cannot authorize that product-state decision.

options.title: Treat requester adoption as delivered
options.body: Accept exact requester consumption as terminal descendant delivery proof and require current-head persisted-state evidence before merge.

options.title: Track consumption separately
options.body: Persist requester consumption without setting terminal delivered status so outward-delivery retry semantics remain independent.

options.title: Defer to durable inbox design
options.body: Pause this PR until the broader completion-spool design defines the canonical delivery-state model.

recommendation.title: Treat requester adoption as delivered
recommendation.body: Accept exact requester consumption as terminal descendant delivery proof and require current-head persisted-state evidence before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history owns both the subagent delivery-state split and current cron execution-versus-delivery semantics.
